skill_title: Predict products of organic reactions (substitution, addition, elimination, esterification, oxidation)
notes: 20 items: 5 lifted-style, 15 fresh. Identify reaction type and predict products: haloalkane substitution/elimination; alkene addition; alcohol elimination/oxidation; esterification.

items.question: Identify the TYPE of organic reaction: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃-CH₃.
items.expectedAnswer: Addition
items.explanation: An alkene C=C becomes a saturated alkane by ADDING H₂ across the double bond. This is an addition (hydrogenation) reaction.

items.question: Identify the TYPE of organic reaction: CH₃-CH₂-Br + NaOH(aq) → CH₃-CH₂-OH + NaBr.
items.expectedAnswer: Substitution
items.explanation: The Br is REPLACED by -OH. One group swaps for another, no change in saturation. This is nucleophilic substitution.

items.question: Identify the TYPE of organic reaction: CH₃-CH₂-OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O (acid catalyst, heat).
items.expectedAnswer: Elimination
items.explanation: A small molecule (H₂O) is removed; a C=C double bond is formed. This is dehydration / elimination.

items.question: Identify the TYPE of reaction: CH₃-COOH + CH₃-CH₂-OH → CH₃-COO-CH₂-CH₃ + H₂O (concentrated H₂SO₄).
items.expectedAnswer: Esterification
items.explanation: Carboxylic acid + alcohol ⇌ ester + water (H₂SO₄ catalyst). This is esterification.

items.question: Predict the product when ethene (CH₂=CH₂) reacts with bromine (Br₂).
items.expectedAnswer: 1,2-dibromoethane (a Br adds to each carbon of the C=C)
items.explanation: Halogenation of alkene by addition: Br₂ adds across the C=C. Product is the corresponding dibromoalkane.
options: 1,2-dibromoethane (a Br adds to each carbon of the C=C)

items.question: Predict the product when propan-1-ol (CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-OH) is dehydrated using concentrated H₂SO₄.
items.expectedAnswer: Propene (water is eliminated, forming a C=C)
items.explanation: Acid-catalysed dehydration removes H₂O, generating an alkene.
options: Propene (water is eliminated, forming a C=C)

items.question: Identify the product of the reaction: CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-Cl + NaOH (concentrated, ethanolic) → ? (elimination conditions).
items.expectedAnswer: Propene (+ NaCl + H₂O) — elimination of HCl
items.explanation: Conditions matter: aqueous NaOH (dilute) → substitution (alcohol); ethanolic NaOH (concentrated) → elimination (alkene).
options: Propan-1-ol — the Cl is substituted by -OH
Propene (+ NaCl + H₂O) — elimination of HCl
Propane — the Cl is simply removed

items.question: Predict the product of CH₃-CH=CH₂ + H₂O (acid catalyst).
items.expectedAnswer: Propan-2-ol (Markovnikov: -OH on the more substituted carbon)
items.explanation: Markovnikov's rule: H goes to the carbon with more Hs, -OH to the carbon with fewer Hs. So 2-ol is the major product.
options: Propan-2-ol (Markovnikov: -OH on the more substituted carbon)

items.question: Predict the product of the OXIDATION of propan-1-ol (CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-OH) using a mild oxidising agent.
items.expectedAnswer: Propanal (the aldehyde; further oxidation would give propanoic acid)
items.explanation: Primary alcohol → aldehyde (mild) → carboxylic acid (strong). Secondary alcohol → ketone (and stops there).
options: Propanal (the aldehyde; further oxidation would give propanoic acid)
Propanone (that comes from a secondary alcohol)
Propanoic acid (that needs strong, not mild, oxidation)

items.question: Predict the oxidation product of propan-2-ol (CH₃-CHOH-CH₃) using a mild oxidising agent.
items.expectedAnswer: Propanone (a secondary alcohol oxidises to a ketone)
items.explanation: Secondary alcohol → ketone. No further oxidation under normal conditions.
options: Propanal (an aldehyde — from a primary alcohol)
Propanone (a secondary alcohol oxidises to a ketone)

items.question: Identify the product of an ESTERIFICATION between ethanoic acid (CH₃-COOH) and methanol (CH₃-OH), with H₂SO₄ catalyst.
items.expectedAnswer: Methyl ethanoate + water
items.explanation: Esterification: R-COOH + R'-OH ⇌ R-COO-R' + H₂O. Ester name: 'alkyl alkanoate' (alkyl from alcohol; alkanoate from acid).
options: Ethyl methanoate + water (the ester named the wrong way round)
Methyl ethanoate only (no water is produced)

items.question: Compare the products: ethane (CH₃-CH₃) reacts with Br₂ in light, vs ethene (CH₂=CH₂) reacts with Br₂ in the dark. What type of reaction is each?
items.expectedAnswer: Ethane: substitution (one H replaced); ethene: addition across the C=C
items.explanation: Saturated (alkane) ⇒ substitution. Unsaturated (alkene) ⇒ addition. Same reagent (Br₂), different mechanism, different product.
options: Ethane: substitution (one H replaced); ethene: addition across the C=C

items.question: Tertiary alcohols (like 2-methylpropan-2-ol, (CH₃)₃C-OH) generally do NOT oxidise under typical conditions. Why?
items.expectedAnswer: The carbon bearing the -OH has no hydrogen to remove, so oxidation cannot occur
items.explanation: Primary (2 Hs on C-OH) → aldehyde → acid. Secondary (1 H) → ketone. Tertiary (0 Hs) → no oxidation.
options: Tertiary alcohols do not contain an -OH group
The carbon bearing the -OH has no hydrogen to remove, so oxidation cannot occur
Tertiary alcohols are too large for the oxidising agent to reach

items.question: Identify the reaction type and products: CH₃-CH₂-CH=CH-CH₃ + HCl → ?
items.expectedAnswer: Addition — HCl adds across the C=C to give chloropentane (a mix of 2- and 3-chloropentane)
items.explanation: Addition of HX across alkene: H to one C, X to the other; Markovnikov's rule (H to C with more H).
options: Substitution — an H is replaced by Cl
Addition — HCl adds across the C=C to give chloropentane (a mix of 2- and 3-chloropentane)

items.question: A learner claims: 'Esterification is irreversible — once you form an ester, it cannot go back to acid + alcohol.' Is this correct?
items.expectedAnswer: Incorrect — esterification is reversible (hydrolysis reverses it: acid + alcohol ⇌ ester + water)
items.explanation: Esterification is an equilibrium reaction. Reverse = ester hydrolysis.
options: Incorrect — esterification is reversible (hydrolysis reverses it: acid + alcohol ⇌ ester + water)
Correct — once formed, an ester cannot revert to acid and alcohol
Correct — esters only break down by combustion, not hydrolysis

items.question: What is the major product of the COMBUSTION of butane (C₄H₁₀) in excess oxygen?
items.expectedAnswer: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water (H₂O)
items.explanation: Complete combustion of hydrocarbons ⇒ CO₂ + H₂O. With limited O₂ you can get CO (incomplete) or even soot.

items.question: Predict the product of the reaction: CH₃-Br + KOH(aq) → ?
items.expectedAnswer: Methanol (CH₃-OH) + KBr — nucleophilic substitution
items.explanation: Aqueous (dilute) KOH/NaOH ⇒ substitution to alcohol. Compare with ethanolic (concentrated) ⇒ elimination to alkene.

items.question: Why is concentrated H₂SO₄ used as a catalyst in BOTH esterification and dehydration of alcohols?
items.expectedAnswer: It protonates the -OH (acid catalyst) and absorbs water, driving both reactions
items.explanation: H₂SO₄ acts as both acid catalyst (mechanism) and desiccant (drives equilibrium by absorbing water).
options: It protonates the -OH (acid catalyst) and absorbs water, driving both reactions
It oxidises the alcohol to speed up the reaction
It supplies the oxygen atoms needed to form the products

items.question: A primary alcohol R-CH₂-OH is fully oxidised. What is the FINAL product?
items.expectedAnswer: A carboxylic acid (R-COOH) — via the aldehyde, then further oxidation
items.explanation: Two-step oxidation chain: 1°-OH → -CHO → -COOH.
options: An aldehyde (that is only the partial/mild oxidation product)
A carboxylic acid (R-COOH) — via the aldehyde, then further oxidation
A ketone (that comes from a secondary alcohol)

items.question: Match the reaction type to its key feature: (a) addition; (b) substitution; (c) elimination; (d) esterification.
items.expectedAnswer: Addition: a small molecule adds across C=C/C≡C; Substitution: one group replaces another on a saturated C; Elimination: a small molecule is removed to form a C=C; Esterification: acid + alcohol → ester + water
items.explanation: Standard CAPS classification of organic reactions.
options: the same, but Addition and Substitution swapped
the same, but Elimination and Esterification swapped

Addition: a small molecule adds across C=C/C≡C; Substitution: one group replaces another on a saturated C; Elimination: a small molecule is removed to form a C=C; Esterification: acid + alcohol → ester + water

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_ADDITION_VS_ELIMINATION: Confuses addition (small molecule added) with elimination (removed)
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_HALOGENATION_PRODUCT: Wrong product for halogenation of alkene
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_HALOALKANE_CONDITIONS: Wrong product depending on conditions (aqueous vs ethanolic)
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_ALCOHOL_OXIDATION: Wrong oxidation product for primary or secondary alcohol
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_CATALYST_ROLE: Can't explain catalyst role in esterification/dehydration
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_TERTIARY_NO_OXIDATION: Doesn't recognise tertiary alcohols don't oxidise
